ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Linezolid: 4

A clinically stable patient treated with intravenous linezolid can swallow and absorb medicines normally. The team considers an oral formulation while maintaining comparable systemic exposure. Which pharmacokinetic property makes this transition feasible when otherwise appropriate?

  1. Increased bacterial drug efflux
  2. Alteration of the ribosomal binding site
  3. High oral bioavailability
  4. Poor systemic absorption after oral administration
  5. Oxygen-dependent bacterial uptake
Answer and explanation

High oral bioavailability

Linezolid has high oral bioavailability, permitting an appropriate IV-to-oral switch in selected stable patients.

Option explanations

High oral bioavailability: Linezolid has high oral bioavailability, permitting an appropriate IV-to-oral switch in selected stable patients.

Poor systemic absorption after oral administration: Oral vancomycin acts mainly in the bowel and does not provide dependable systemic therapy. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Oxygen-dependent bacterial uptake: Aminoglycosides require active oxygen-dependent transport into susceptible bacteria. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Increased bacterial drug efflux: Efflux can lower intracellular tetracycline concentrations and cause resistance. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Alteration of the ribosomal binding site: Ribosomal methylation or other target changes can reduce binding of some protein-synthesis inhibitors. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
